key_insight: An automated whole-slide histopathology segmentation pipeline with adaptive augmentation and multi-resolution ensembling improved colorectal cancer grade detection and normal mucosa labeling.
clinical_relevance: This could help speed up pathology workflows and support earlier, more consistent colorectal cancer assessment after biopsy.
method: Dense prediction transformers with multiple encoder backbones segmented overlapping patches from whole-slide images.
Training used an adaptive augmentation policy guided by large language models.
Top models were combined with soft voting and refined using Gaussian blur, morphological closing, and connected components analysis.
evidence_signal: On a colorectal cancer grade dataset, the reported F1 score improved from 62.92 to 69.84 after the full approach.
watch_item: Performance is reported on a specific dataset, so generalization to other slide sources, scanners, and staining protocols still needs external validation.
paper_title: Colorectal Cancer Segmentation with Adaptive Augmentation and Multi-Resolution Ensemble Models
